problem: Find the directional derivative of the function $f(x,y)=x{e}^{y}+{x}^{2}y$ at the point $A(1,0)$ in the direction towards the point $B(0,1).$

feedback.problem: Find the directional derivative of the function $f(x,y)=6{x}^{2}+2y$ at the point $(0,1)$ in the direction of the vector $v=3i+5j.$
feedback.worked_solution:
The directional derivative ${f}_{u}^{′}(a,b)$ of a function $f(x,y)$ at the point $(a,b)$ in the direction of the vector $v$ is given by

$$
{f}_{u}^{′}(a,b)=∇f(a,b)\cdot u
$$

where $u$ is a unit vector in the direction of $v.$

First, we find the unit vector $u$ in the direction of $v:$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖v‖ & =\sqrt{{3}^{2}+{5}^{2}}=\sqrt{34} \\ u & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{34}}(3i+5j)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute the gradient $∇f(x,y)$ and evaluate it at the point $(0,1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\,f(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(6{x}^{2}+2y)\text{ }i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(6{x}^{2}+2y)\text{ }j \\  & =12x\,i+2\,j \\ ∇\,f(0,1) & =(12\cdot 0)\,i+2\,j \\  & =2j\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the directional derivative is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{u}^{′}(0,1) & =∇\,f(0,1)\cdot u \\  & =2j\cdot (\frac{3}{\sqrt{34}}i+\frac{5}{\sqrt{34}}j) \\  & =\frac{0\cdot 3+2\cdot 5}{\sqrt{34}} \\  & =\frac{10\sqrt{34}}{34}.\end{aligned}
$$
